target.title: fix(gmail): enforce per-account no-send guard before dry-run exit
target.body:
Fixes #915.

The per-account no-send guard (`gog config no-send set <email>`) is enforced only inside each send command's `Run()`, after `requireGmailSendService` resolves auth. Every send path calls `dryRunExit` before that point, so `--dry-run` never evaluates the guard and reports `would gmail.send` for an account whose sends are blocked. The other two guard layers (`--gmail-no-send`, config `gmail_no_send`) are enforced pre-`Run()` in `enforceGmailNoSend` and block under `--dry-run`, so the three layers disagreed about the same invariant.

Real sends were never at risk: `checkAccountNoSend` still blocks before any API call on the non-dry-run path. The bug is the safety signal — a `--dry-run` probe is exactly how an operator or agent verifies a guard, and it reported the guard as absent.

This enforces the per-account guard in `enforceGmailNoSend` alongside the flag and global config checks. The account resolves without auth via `requireAccount` (flag → `GOG_ACCOUNT` → configured default, with alias resolution from config). When no account is resolvable, the check is skipped: the command owns that failure mode, and the existing post-auth `checkAccountNoSend` remains as defense-in-depth.

## Before / after

With `{"no_send_accounts": {"blocked@example.com": true}}` in config:

```text
# v0.34.0
$ gog gmail send --account blocked@example.com --to a@example.com --subject S --body B --dry-run
Dry run: would gmail.send

# this branch
$ gog gmail send --account blocked@example.com --to a@example.com --subject S --body B --dry-run
Gmail sending is blocked for blocked@example.com (config no-send)
```

No over-blocking: a non-guarded account still dry-runs normally, and non-send commands (`gmail drafts create`) still work for the guarded account.

## Test plan

- [x] `TestConfigNoSendAccountBlocksBeforeDryRun` — all four guarded send paths blocked under `--dry-run` (fails on unpatched main, passes with fix)
- [x] `TestConfigNoSendAccountDoesNotOverblockDryRun` — other accounts and non-send commands unaffected
- [x] `go test ./internal/cmd/ -run NoSend` — all existing no-send coverage passes
- [x] `make test` — full suite passes
- [x] `make fmt` — no changes
- [x] `make lint` — clean

User-facing change: `--dry-run` on a send command now reports the per-account block instead of `Dry run: would gmail.send`. No new flags.
